extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, peer reviewers, and open science advocates
extracted.subtask_description: A concise definition and taxonomy of 'open peer review' (OPR), listing the distinct traits or practices by which traditional peer review can be adapted to align with Open Science principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPR definition (umbrella term)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open peer review is an umbrella term for a number of overlapping ways that peer review models can be adapted in line with the aims of Open Science, including making reviewer and author identities open, publishing review reports and enabling greater participation in the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames OPR as a multi-trait concept rather than a single practice; sets the scope for the subsequent listed traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors and reviewers are aware of each other’s identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies removal of anonymity between authors and reviewers; can affect accountability and social dynamics of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Review reports are published alongside the relevant article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Makes reviewer evaluations visible to readers and the community; supports transparency and reuse of review content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The wider community [is] able to contribute to the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opens reviewing beyond invited experts to broader community comment or crowd-reviewing models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct reciprocal discussion between author(s) and reviewers, and/or between reviewers, is allowed and encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages dialogic exchanges (e.g., discussion threads, rebuttals, iterative review) rather than unidirectional reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open pre-review manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are made immediately available (e.g., via pre-print servers like arXiv) in advance of any formal peer review procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates early dissemination and informal community feedback prior to formal peer review; example given: arXiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open final-version commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Review or commenting on final “version of record” publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows post-publication critique and annotation on the formally published record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open platforms ("decoupled review")
rubrics_metrics.description: Review is facilitated by a different organizational entity than the venue of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separates the review service from the journal/publisher (e.g., independent review platforms), enabling review to be portable or re-used across venues.
